commentary:
Energy is the story this morning: Brent is down 2.9% to $86 and WTI off 2.5% to just above $80 after reports that Iran and Oman are pushing talks toward an "interim" reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, with Saudi Aramco reportedly offering more barrels routed outside the Strait — a double hit to the supply-risk premium. A 4.2m-bbl API crude build compounded the move, and the curve confirms it: Brent's prompt spread has slumped to its weakest since mid-July and implied vol keeps bleeding lower.

Products are leading the way down — gasoil off nearly 5%, heating oil -3.3% — though European gasoline cracks remain at multi-month highs, so watch refined spreads rather than flat price for the cleaner signal. TTF fell 3% in sympathy. The broader tone is cautious rather than risk-off: US index futures are flat-to-lower as traders sit on their hands ahead of Nvidia earnings — the key test of the AI trade's durability — and the July PCE inflation print. Rates are the tension point: ECB's Schnabel says rates must rise further on inflation risks, while in the US the Treasury's buyback interventions are on a collision course with the Warsh Fed's inflation fight, and positioning against long bonds looks crowded enough to squeeze, according to reports.

Gold has eased off a three-month high awaiting Jackson Hole clarity. Elsewhere, wheat is up 1.6% across both boards and coffee is unwinding hard (-2.5% robusta). Watch EIA stocks, PCE, Nvidia, then Jackson Hole.
